Captured around 1959, this photograph shows Miles Davis recording at New York City's 30th Street Studios, the legendary space where some of jazz's most enduring recordings took shape. Produced by Sonic Editions, the print is made to order and custom-framed by hand, with archival photographic paper and conservation-grade materials chosen to preserve the image. Each edition is individually numbered and includes the story behind the photograph on the reverse.

entry.content:
JBL introduced the L150 speaker in 1979 as a walnut tower with a 12-inch woofer. The new L150 Classic, the flagship of its current Classic Series, is inspired by that 70s original but steps up to a 15-inch woofer, wider than a vinyl record, paired with a 6.5-inch midrange and a 1-inch titanium-dome tweeter. The cabinet dresses the part in natural walnut veneer and a vintage-style black foam grille that attaches with magnets. Front-panel controls adjust the bass and treble in precise steps, so you can dial in your own balance.

entry.content:
Six identical pieces come together to form something that looks less like a traditional puzzle and more like an object from another dimension. Craighill's Andromeda reworks the classic six-piece burr puzzle with shifting symmetry, subtle spirals, and a form that refuses to settle into a familiar geometric category. Heat-forged aluminum gives each piece the precision needed for its intricate interlocking construction, while a black anodized finish emphasizes the near-fractal surface. Designed by George I. Bell, it's a dense mechanical puzzle that's as interesting to hold and examine as it is difficult to solve.

entry.content:
Jack London's The Call of the Wild remains one of the greatest adventure novels ever written, following the unforgettable journey of Buck, a powerful St. Bernard-Shepherd mix thrust from a comfortable life into the unforgiving wilderness of the Klondike Gold Rush. As Buck learns to survive among sled dogs and harsh northern landscapes, he gradually sheds the comforts of domestication and answers the instinctive pull of the wild. Equal parts thrilling adventure and timeless meditation on resilience, freedom, and identity, it is a classic that continues to resonate with readers more than a century after its publication.

entry.title: Joe DiMaggio's Patek Philippe 130 Chronograph Watch
entry.summary: In 1941, Joe DiMaggio got a hit in 56 straight games for the New York Yankees, a record that still stands. The Yankees are believed to have given him this Patek Philippe Reference 130 chronograph in 1948, and a 1949 photo of DiMaggio with actress Myrna Dell at New York's Stork Cl
entry.content:
In 1941, Joe DiMaggio got a hit in 56 straight games for the New York Yankees, a record that still stands. The Yankees are believed to have given him this Patek Philippe Reference 130 chronograph in 1948, and a 1949 photo of DiMaggio with actress Myrna Dell at New York's Stork Club appears to show it on his wrist. The 33mm case is 18-karat yellow gold and may never have been polished, and the dial is marked with hand-cut Breguet numerals, a classic style with rounded, open strokes. DiMaggio kept the watch until his death in 1999, and his estate sold it in 2006 to benefit the Joe DiMaggio Children's Hospital Foundation. It has had only three owners and is now for sale.

entry.content:
Greta Grossman's Model 6200 desk is one of the defining pieces of postwar California modernism, combining Scandinavian discipline with the lighter, more experimental language of Southern California design. Designed in 1952 for Glenn of California, the asymmetrical composition pairs a broad black writing surface with a suspended walnut storage cabinet, diagonal tapered leg, and slender iron supports. This original period example carries extraordinary provenance from the estate of jazz legend Dave Brubeck, whose music similarly explored rhythm, balance, and unexpected structure. Professionally presented with its original character intact, it remains a remarkable piece of mid-century design history.
